translation_en: Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Salm ibn Zarir narrated to us. I heard Abu Raja’ say: ‘Imran ibn Husayn narrated to us that they were with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on a journey. They travelled through the night. At daybreak they stopped to rest, and sleep overcame them until the sun had risen high. The first to wake from his sleep was Abu Bakr. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was not woken from his sleep until he woke by himself. ‘Umar woke, and Abu Bakr sat at the Prophet’s head and began saying “Allah is greatest” and raising his voice until the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, woke. He got down and led us in the morning prayer. One man from the group stayed apart and did not pray with us. When the Prophet had finished, he said, “So-and-so, what kept you from praying with us?” The man said, “I was in a state of major ritual impurity.” He told him to perform dry ablution with clean earth. Then he prayed. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, placed me among the riders in front of him. We were extremely thirsty. As we travelled, we came upon a woman with her legs hanging between two water-skins. We asked her, “Where is the water?” She said, “There is no water.” We asked, “How far is it from your family to the water?” She said, “A day and a night.” We said, “Come with us to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.” She said, “Who is the Messenger of Allah?” We could not let her decide what to do; we took her to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. She told him what she had told us, except that she also told him she was a widow. He ordered her two water-skins to be brought and rubbed the openings. We drank while thirsty, forty men, until we were satisfied. We filled every waterskin and water-container we had with us, but we did not water a single camel. Her water-skins were almost dripping from being so full. Then he said, “Bring what you have.” They gathered for her the broken pieces of food and dates. When she reached her people, she said, “I have met either the greatest magician of people, or he is a prophet, as they claim.” Through that woman, Allah guided that clan, and she and they embraced Islam.’”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah said to Umm Sulaym, “I heard the voice of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sounding weak. I recognize hunger in it. Do you have anything?” She said, “Yes.” She brought out some barley rolls, then took her head-covering and wrapped part of it around the bread. She tucked it under my arm and tied part of it around me, then sent me to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. I went with it and found the Messenger of Allah in the mosque with the people. I stood near them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to me, “Did Abu Talhah send you?” I said, “Yes.” He asked, “With food?” I said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to those with him, “Get up.” He set out, and I went ahead of them until I came to Abu Talhah and told him. Abu Talhah said, “Umm Sulaym, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has brought the people, and we have nothing to feed them.” She said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” Abu Talhah went until he met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Then the Messenger of Allah came with Abu Talhah. He said, “Umm Sulaym, bring what you have.” She brought that bread. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ordered it to be broken into pieces. Umm Sulaym squeezed out some fat from a small skin-container and used it as a relish. Then the Messenger of Allah said over it whatever Allah willed him to say. Then he said, “Let ten people come in.” Abu Talhah let them in. They ate until they were full, then went out. He said again, “Let ten people come in.” Abu Talhah let them in. They ate until they were full, then went out. He said again, “Let ten people come in.” Abu Talhah let them in. They ate until they were full, then went out. Then he said, “Let ten people come in.” The whole group ate and were satisfied. There were seventy or eighty men.’”

Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us, from his father. Abu ‘Uthman narrated to us that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, told him that the people of the Suffah were poor. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, once said, “Whoever has food for two should take a third person with him, and whoever has food for four should take a fifth or a sixth,” or words to that effect. Abu Bakr came with three people, and the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went out with ten. Abu Bakr and three people [also came]. The narrator said: I was one of them, along with my father and my mother. I do not know whether he also said my wife and my servant. We were between our house and Abu Bakr’s house. Abu Bakr ate the evening meal with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, then stayed until he had prayed the night prayer. He returned and stayed until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had eaten the evening meal. He came back after as much of the night had passed as Allah willed. His wife said to him, “What kept you from your guests?” He asked, “Have you not served them their evening meal?” She said, “They refused until you came. They offered it to them, but they refused.” I went away and hid. Abu Bakr said, “You fool!” He rebuked and insulted me, then said, “Eat!” and swore, “By Allah, I will never eat it.” By Allah, whenever we took a morsel, the food grew from underneath it, becoming more than it had been, until they were full. It had become more than before. Abu Bakr looked and saw that it was as much as before, or more. He said to his wife, “Sister of Banu Firas, is it more?” She said, “No, by the comfort of my eyes, it is now three times more than it was before.” Abu Bakr ate some of it and said, “That oath was from Satan”—meaning his own oath. Then he ate a morsel and carried the food to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. It was still with him in the morning. There was a truce between us and a people, and its term ended. We separated into twelve groups, with people accompanying each man. Allah knows how many were with each man. The narrator said that he sent the food with them, and they all ate from it, or words to that effect. Another narrator says, “We knew that through the group leaders.”

Musa said: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to me, and I think this was related to him from Ibn ‘Umar: Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl went to Syria to ask about religion and follow it. He met a Jewish scholar and asked him about their religion. He said, “Perhaps I will follow your religion, so tell me about it.” The scholar said, “You cannot follow our religion until you take your share of Allah’s anger.” Zayd said, “I flee only from Allah’s anger, and I will never take any share of Allah’s anger. How could I bear it? Can you direct me to another religion?” The scholar said, “I know of none, unless it is that you become a hanif.” Zayd said, “What is a hanif?” He said, “The religion of Ibrahim: he was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and he worshipped none but Allah.” Zayd left and met a Christian scholar. He asked him the same, and the man said, “You cannot follow our religion until you take your share of Allah’s curse.” Zayd said, “I flee only from Allah’s curse. I will never take any share of Allah’s curse or His anger. How could I bear it? Can you direct me to another religion?” He said, “I know of none, unless it is that you become a hanif.” Zayd asked, “What is a hanif?” He said, “The religion of Ibrahim: he was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and he worshipped none but Allah.” When Zayd saw how they described Ibrahim, peace be upon him, he left. When he came out into the open, he raised his hands and said, “O Allah, I bear witness that I follow the religion of Ibrahim.”

Abu al-Nu‘man narrated to us: Abu ‘Awanah narrated to us, from Bayan Abu Bishr, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abu Bakr entered upon a woman from the tribe of Ahmas named Zaynab. He saw that she was not speaking and asked, “Why is she not speaking?” They said, “She came on pilgrimage while keeping silent.” He said to her, “Speak, for this is not lawful. This is one of the practices of the time of ignorance.” So she spoke and asked, “Who are you?” He said, “A man from the Emigrants.” She asked, “Which of the Emigrants?” He said, “From Quraysh.” She asked, “Which part of Quraysh are you from?” He said, “You ask many questions. I am Abu Bakr.” She asked, “How long will we remain upon this good way that Allah brought us after the time of ignorance?” He said, “You will remain upon it as long as your leaders remain upright among you.” She asked, “Who are the leaders?” He said, “Did your people not have chiefs and leading men who would command them and whom they would obey?” She said, “Yes.” He said, “Those are the leaders over the people.”

Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra’ narrated to me: ‘Ali ibn Mushir informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her. She said: A black woman belonging to some Arabs accepted Islam, and she had a small shelter in the mosque. She used to come to us and talk with us. Whenever she finished speaking, she would say, “The day of the leather sash is one of the wonders of our Lord. Indeed, He rescued me from the land of disbelief.” After she repeated this often, ‘Aishah said to her, “What was the day of the sash?” She said, “A young girl from my family went out wearing a sash made of leather. It fell from her, and a kite swooped down on it, thinking it was meat. It took it away. They accused me of taking it and tortured me, until things went so far that they searched my private parts. While they were gathered around me and I was in distress, the kite came until it was level with our heads, then dropped the sash. They took it, and I said to them, ‘This is what you accused me of taking, but I was innocent of it.’”

Abu Ma‘mar narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Qatan Abu al-Haytham narrated to us: Abu Yazid al-Madani narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. He said: The first case of sworn testimony in a murder in the time of ignorance was among us, the Banu Hashim. A man from Banu Hashim was hired by a man from another branch of Quraysh. He went with the man and his camels. A man from Banu Hashim passed by him, and the strap of his saddlebag had broken. He said, “Help me with a rope-ring so I can fasten the strap of my saddlebag and the camels will not scatter.” The man gave him a rope-ring, and he fastened the strap of his saddlebag with it. When they stopped, all the camels were tied except one. The man who had hired him said, “What is the matter with this camel? Why was it the only one among the camels that was not tied?” He said, “It has no rope-ring.” The man threw a stick at him, and that was the cause of his death. A man from Yemen passed by him and asked, “Will you attend the season?” He said, “I do not attend it, though I may attend it sometimes.” He asked, “Will you deliver a message from me at some time?” The man said, “Yes.” He said, “When you attend the season, call out, ‘People of Quraysh!’ When they answer you, call out, ‘People of Banu Hashim!’ If they answer you, ask for Abu Talib and tell him that so-and-so killed me over a rope-ring.” The hired man died. When the man who had hired him arrived, Abu Talib came to him and asked, “What happened to our companion?” He said, “He fell ill, and I took good care of him. I was the one who buried him.” Abu Talib said, “That was what could be expected of you.” Some time passed. Then the man who had been entrusted with delivering the message attended the season and called, “People of Quraysh!” They said, “Here are Quraysh.” He called, “People of Banu Hashim!” They said, “Here are Banu Hashim.” He asked, “Where is Abu Talib?” They said, “Here is Abu Talib.” He said, “So-and-so charged me to deliver you a message: so-and-so killed him over a rope-ring.” Abu Talib went to him and said, “Choose one of three options: you may pay one hundred camels, for you killed our companion; or fifty men from your people may swear that you did not kill him; if you refuse, we will kill you for him.” The man went to his people and said, “We will swear.” A woman from Banu Hashim, who had been married to a man from among them and had borne him a son, came and said, “Abu Talib, I would like you to exempt my son from one of the fifty men, and not make him take the oath where the oaths are taken.” He did so. Then one of the men came to Abu Talib and said, “You wanted fifty men to swear instead of one hundred camels, which would be two camels for each man. Here are my two camels; accept them on my behalf, and do not make me take the oath where the oaths are taken.” Abu Talib accepted them, and forty-eight men came and swore. Ibn ‘Abbas said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, before a year had passed, not one of those forty-eight had an eye that blinked.

‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: al-Muthanna narrated to us, from Abu Jamrah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. He said: When Abu Dharr heard that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had been sent, he said to his brother, “Ride to this valley and find out about this man who claims to be a prophet and receives news from heaven. Listen to some of what he says, then come back to me.” His brother set out until he reached him and heard some of his words. Then he returned to Abu Dharr and said, “I saw him commanding noble character, and I heard speech that is not poetry.” Abu Dharr said, “You have not satisfied what I wanted to know.” He packed provisions and took a worn waterskin filled with water until he reached Makkah. He went to the mosque and looked for the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, but did not know him. He disliked asking about him. When part of the night had passed, ‘Ali saw him and recognized that he was a stranger. When ‘Ali saw him, he followed him. Neither of them asked the other anything until morning. Then Abu Dharr took his waterskin and provisions to the mosque and stayed there that day. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not see him before evening. He returned to his sleeping place. ‘Ali passed by him and said, “Has it not occurred to this man to find out where he is staying?” He got him up and took him along. Neither of them asked the other anything until the third day. ‘Ali came back in the same way and had him stay with him. Then he said, “Will you tell me what brought you here?” He said, “If you give me a solemn promise that you will guide me, I will tell you.” ‘Ali did so, and Abu Dharr told him. ‘Ali said, “It is true. He is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. In the morning, follow me. If I see anything that makes me fear for you, I will stand as if I were relieving myself. If I continue walking, follow me until you enter where I enter.” Abu Dharr did that. He followed him until he entered upon the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and went in with him. He heard some of his words and accepted Islam then and there. The Prophet said to him, “Return to your people and tell them, until my command comes to you.” He said, “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will proclaim it among them.” He went out until he came to the mosque and called at the top of his voice, “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” The people got up and beat him until they knocked him down. Al-‘Abbas came and threw himself over him, saying, “Woe to you! Do you not know that he is from Ghifar and that your trade route to Syria passes by them?” He rescued him from them. The next day Abu Dharr returned and did the same. They beat him and rushed at him, and al-‘Abbas threw himself over him.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma‘il, from Qays, who said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl say in the mosque of Kufa, “By Allah, I remember that ‘Umar had tied me up because of Islam before ‘Umar himself became Muslim. If Uhud were to split apart because of what you did to ‘Uthman, it would have deserved to split apart.”

Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Ibn Wahb said: ‘Umar ibn Muhammad narrated to me: My grandfather, Zayd ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, informed me, from his father, who said: While ‘Umar was in his house, afraid, al-‘As ibn Wa’il al-Sahmi, Abu ‘Amr, came to him. He was wearing a fine patterned robe and a shirt edged with silk. He was from Banu Sahm, who had been our allies in the time of ignorance. He said to ‘Umar, “What is the matter with you?” ‘Umar said, “Your people claim that they will kill me if I become Muslim.” He said, “No one can get to you.” After he said that, I felt safe. Al-‘As went out and met the people, who had filled the valley. He asked, “Where are you going?” They said, “We are going after this Ibn al-Khattab who has left his religion.” He said, “No one can get to him.” So the people turned back.
